summary: K. Sambasiva Sastri (1879–1946) was an Indology scholar. He succeeded T. Ganapati Sastri and served as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library from circa 1928 to 1939.

K. Srinivasan is an Indologist who served as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College and held the Brahmasri Anna Subramaniam Chair at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020–2026).

K. V. Puttappa (1904–1994) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He was educated at Hardwick High School and College, Maharaja's College, Mysore (circa 1925–1929), and the University of Mysore (circa 1927–1929).

K. V. Raman (1934–2024) studied at Madras Christian College under A. J. Boyd, the University of Madras, and the Institute of Archaeology. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (circa 1957–1976) and chaired Ancient History and Archaeology at Madras (1976–1995).

K. V. Ramesh (1935–2013) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Secretary of the Epigraphical Society of India, Director of Epigraphy at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1981–1987), and Honorary Director at ORI Mysore (attested 2012).
K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar (1880–1960) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Principal of Banaras Hindu University and Central Hindu College from circa 1935 to 1938.

K. Venkata Ramanan studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang, at Visva-Bharati under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and at the Harvard-Yenching Institute. He taught in Buddhist studies and philosophy at Visva-Bharati University.

id: P:Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso
summary: Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Kaie Mochizuki (born 1959) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. His career includes serving as a professor of Buddhism (attested 2015) and university president (attested 2026) at Minobusan University.
Kaigen Noritake is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kenyu Mitomo. He served as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaikyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) studied under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. In Buddhist studies and Indology, he held professorships at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho universities, and served as principal of Shiba Junior & Senior High School (circa 1925–1933).

Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934) studied at Komazawa and Keio universities. Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he lectured at Harvard (circa 1913–1915), held posts at Soto-shu University, and served as headteacher and the first president of Komazawa University (1925–1934).
Kaiun Shirodate worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and professor (attested 1999–2002) at Otani University.

Kakichi Kadowaki (1926–2017) studied at the University of Tokyo and under Sogen Omori. Working in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, he was on the faculty at Sophia University from circa 1970 to 1996.

Kakushō Ujiie (died 1985) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who conducted research studies at Tribhuvan University and served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1970, 1984–1985).

Kali Kinkar Datta (1905–1982) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Honorary Director (attested 1959–1966) and Joint Director (attested 1987) of K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute and as Vice-Chancellor of Patna University (attested 1973).

Kalidas Nag (1891–1966) studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. An Indologist and historian, he held posts at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta (circa 1923–1955), and served as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society (circa 1942–1946).
Kalpana K. Sheth is an Indologist who completed her doctorate under Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani and held a post at the L.D. Institute of Indology.

Kalu Rinpoche (1905–1989) studied at Palpung Monastery and Dechen Ösel Ling under gurus including Khakyab Dorje and Norbu Tondrup. In Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he served as Vajra Master at Palpung and Abbot of Changchub Choeling Monastery (1957).
Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is an Indology and Sinology scholar who studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He served as an emeritus professor at the University of Windsor (attested 2002).
